insight: The map shows a solar potential score for each municipality on a 0‑100 scale. Scores are high where the sun shines strongly and the sky stays clear. For example, City of San Pedro in Laguna, Mandaue City and Pilar in Cebu all score 100, reflecting about 5 kWh/m² of daily sunlight and warm temperatures around 26‑28 °C. The score does not depend on how close a town is to a volcano or the sea; those features are not part of the calculation. Even places near water or on volcanic islands can have lower scores if clouds, hills or local shading block the sun. Calayan in Cagayan scores 0, showing very little usable sunlight. Santiago in Ilocos Sur, despite being on the coast, scores only 60.6 because its average solar radiation is about 3.7 kWh/m² per day, lower than the very high areas. General Nakar in Quezon, also near mountains, still reaches a high score of 61.8 thanks to decent irradiance. Overall, 532 municipalities are classified as high and 466 as very high, while only one each fall into moderate and very low categories.
